feature: Every handle says what it does
summary: Rest the pointer on any handle around a selected object and it now says what a press would do before you press it: the matching resize arrows on the eight handles round a layer or the picture, a curved arrow on the knob that turns it, and an open hand on the ends of a line or arrow, which used to be the odd ones out beside a measurement's feet.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. One flag, "Every handle says what it does", on by default.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press R, and drag out a rectangle.
Press V, then move the pointer slowly over each of the eight small squares round it without pressing.
Move onto the round knob floating above its top edge.
Drag that knob to turn the box, then run the pointer round its eight handles again.
Press A, drag an arrow, press Escape to skip the caption, then rest the pointer on each end of it.
Click the picture's row named Canvas in the Layers list, then rest on a corner of the picture itself.
Click empty space to pick nothing, and go back over all of those spots.

evaluate: Over a resize handle, do the arrows point the way you expect to be able to drag it?
Does the turn arrow read as "this rotates" at a glance, and does it look like it belongs beside the resize arrows?
On a turned box, does the pointer match where the handle SITS rather than what it was called before the turn?
Is the open hand right for the two ends of an arrow, or would you rather they behaved like resize handles?
Does anything now flicker or feel busy while you move across a selection?
rough: The turn arrow is drawn by us, because the platform ships no rotate pointer. The four resize pointers are the system's own, so they will always match a Finder window. The third picture beside this audit is the five of them side by side, since a screen capture never contains the pointer itself.
Opposite handles wear the same picture: top and bottom both show up-and-down arrows, because the platform draws one pointer per axis, not one per handle. That is the native behaviour, not a shortcut.

Hold Option over a corner and the press SKEWS rather than resizes, but the pointer still shows resize arrows. Left alone: there is no conventional skew pointer to reach for, and inventing one felt worse than saying nothing.

A LOCKED layer still shows its handles and still resizes from them, so the pointer says so too rather than lying about the press. That is a real hole in what locking means, and it is now its own task rather than something quietly changed here.

The Crop tool keeps its plain crosshair over its own eight handles. Crop is its own mode with its own pointer, so whether the crosshair should give way is a judgement of its own, filed as a separate task.

Verified on the real app through Scripts/playtest/grab-cue.json, which now walks 34 pointer stages. The probe holds Screen Recording, so the two app pictures here are real screen captures. They show the handles, not the pointer: no screen capture contains the pointer, so the pointer itself is proved by the walk's log rather than by a picture.
